newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end mixed on uncertainties.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end mixed on uncertainties.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mixed on Wednesday on market uncertainties, traders said.
The most actively traded September 1997 contract ended at an intraday low of 3,285 yuan ($396) per tonne, losing 10 yuan. It opened at 3,350 yuan per tonne and hit a high of 3,356 yuan.
May rose 27 yuan to 3,292, July 58 to 3,318, November fell nine to 3,379 and the January 1998 contract was unchanged at 3,380 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume rose to 21,000 tonnes from 19,000 tonne.
Soybeans opened mixed and fluctuated in a wide range for most of the session, traders said.
"Investors were mixed about short-term market trend, and that led to today's fluctuations," one trader said.
"Large speculative buying emerged at low levels today, indicating soybeans will not fall sharply in the next few days," he said.
Traders said they expected soybeans to consolidate around current levels in the next few days.
